bottleneck.description: World's largest unit-volume producer of digital industrial cameras (area-scan, line-scan, 3D, embedded vision), but heavily dependent on Sony CMOS sensors and competing with Teledyne, IDS, JAI, Allied Vision, Hikvision.

dependency.key_customers: Cognex (board-level), machine vision integrators, factory automation OEMs, life-science/medical imaging, retail/traffic
dependency.key_suppliers: Sony (Pregius/IMX CMOS image sensors), onsemi, FPGAs, optical lenses

editorial.notes: Basler is the largest unit-volume maker of industrial machine-vision cameras in Europe, but the camera segment is highly contested by Teledyne DALSA, Sony, IDS, JAI, Allied Vision/FLIR, Hikvision/Hikrobot and Toshiba Teli. Basler is actually downstream of Sony's Pregius/IMX CMOS sensor monopoly-ish position; cameras are a mid-stack commodity-leaning subsystem with many substitution paths. No structural bottleneck — clear LOW.
